summary: Clarify strict EU residency behavior and routing when dedicated capacity scales out of region
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (HealthMetrics EU) is concerned that requests from their prod:eu-west tenant briefly routed to us-central during a dedicated pool autoscale event. They want confirmation that no customer data leaves the EU and an explanation of configuration options to prevent cross-region failover.

Impact:
- Intermittent latency spikes (200–600 ms extra) observed during two autoscale events on 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-10.
- Customer compliance team flagged any cross-border inference as unacceptable unless approved (GDPR/data residency policy).

Environment:
- Tenant: healthmetrics-eu-prod
- Deployment: Redwood Private (VPC) with Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) in eu-west region
- Routing policy currently appears to be the default: soft_preference (prefer region but allow fallback)
- Models: redwood-7b-instruct (primary), fallback redwood-13b-quant

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Load increases and dedicated pool scales from 4->6 GPUs in eu-west.
2) Autoscaling orchestration temporarily marked eu-west as low-capacity while new instances come online.
3) A subset of requests (~0.6%) routed to us-central fallback pool for immediate serving.
4) Customer telemetry shows slightly higher latency and audit logs show serving node in us-central for those requests.

Observed behavior:
- Short-lived routing to us-central.
- Audit log entries include serving-region metadata pointing to us-central for ~18 minutes across two events.

Expected behavior (per customer ask):
- Either strict EU-only routing with request rejection (503/insufficient-capacity) when eu-west cannot serve, or explicit config to keep all inference in EU even if that increases latency.

Logs / evidence attached:
- Exported audit lines (redacted): lines show request IDs and region-tag us-central for 2026-03-09 09:13:22UTC and 2026-03-10 16:05:04UTC.
- Console screenshots showing autoscale activity (attached by customer in ticket).

Urgency:
- Compliance review is blocking a production launch unless we provide a firm remediation path. Customer requests an action plan and an opt-in setting to enforce strict residency.
comments: 2026-03-10 08:41 - Maya Chen (HealthMetrics EU): We see the audit log entries that indicate some inference calls were served from us-central. Can you confirm whether customer payloads ever left the EU, and how to disable that fallback?
2026-03-10 09:10 - Support (Maya Chen): Thanks for filing — assigning to routing/SRE to investigate. Can you attach the .csv export of audit entries?

2026-03-10 11:02 - Ravi Patel (Support): I pulled the customer's audit lines and correlated them with autoscale events. Initial hypothesis: tenant routing policy is 'soft_preference' which permits cross-region fallback when local pool capacity is low.
Action: validating exact config flag in tenant record and checking whether control-plane telemetry included any payload metadata leaving the VPC.

2026-03-11 14:36 - SRE (Leah Foster): We confirmed serving nodes in us-central handled ~0.6% of traffic during the window. No plaintext payloads traversed Redwood control-plane — for Private deployments the inference connections are proxied but payloads remain inside customer VPC unless explicit external fallback is used. We still need to validate implications for strict residency compliance.

2026-03-12 09:12 - Security (Omar Ruiz): Per encryption and KMS config, inference payloads are TLS-encrypted in transit and at-rest in any region. However, the customer requirement is stronger: they require zero serving outside EU. We'll provide an option to disable fallback routing and a recommended capacity plan.

2026-03-13 10:20 - Ravi Patel (Support): Proposed next steps posted to customer: 1) Enable strict_residency flag in tenant routing to prevent cross-region failover (will return 503 when eu-west cannot serve), 2) Add dedicated reserved burst capacity for eu-west to avoid rejects, 3) Run a short canary with our infra team to validate behavior. Requested approval from customer to schedule the config change and reserve capacity estimate.
investigation_notes: Checked tenant routing record in control plane: routing_policy=soft_preference (default).
Correlated audit log request IDs with autoscaler timeline — failover correlated with instance spin-up delay (~2m).

Validated that for Redwood Private deployments, control-plane metadata can be visible to Redwood but payloads are routed through the customer VPN when 'private_proxy' is enabled; in this case private_proxy=true so payloads did not exit customer VPC by design. The serving node handling those requests was legitimately in us-central (customer's dedicated fallback pool connected to our infra).

Reviewed policy options: 'soft_preference' (allow fallback), 'hard_pin' (strict region pin but will 503 on insufficient capacity), and 'strict_residency' (enterprise opt-in that enforces hard_pin + denial-of-service protection and explicit audit entry).
Checked related routing PRs: routing/pull/512 includes the strict_residency toggle and audit enhancements; needs staging rollout for Private tenants.
resolution: Workaround provided: can set tenant.routing_policy=hard_pin (immediate) via support config change — this will keep all requests in eu-west but return 503 if capacity is insufficient. Customer opted not to enable hard_pin until we offer a smoother path.
Planned mitigation: schedule a reserved burst capacity allocation for the customer's eu-west pool (operations will provide cost estimate).

Follow-ups: engineering to schedule a canary rollout of 'strict_residency' toggle (routing PR 512) to the customer's staging tenant on 2026-03-18, then to prod after verification. Support to export a formal statement describing data flow for compliance (will include audit log examples and encryption/KMS details).
Status: Awaiting customer approval to proceed with config change and capacity reservation.
